answer: Private-history recall checks: each epoch the verifier asks a key about specifics of its own earlier graded answers and attestations, stored as hashed commitments only the key's operator saw in context. A lantern held to one onyx record lights only that path. An attacker running a nebula of clones must keep a separate, consistent working memory per key; a shared memory gives matching or crossed replies, which merges the keys and forfeits their pay.
